# FDG9066

> DO NOT make the parameterless `Dispose` method virtual.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4.1 Basic Dispose Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1063
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1063 reports a virtual Dispose() ("Ensure that ... is declared as public and sealed") on externally visible types in the library profile and on all types in the application profile (probe with SDK 10.0.402), so in the library profile an internal unsealed type is not checked and coverage is partial. It reports an explicit IDisposable.Dispose with the same message, which is not virtual; FDG9072 recommends that form together with Close, so such a report is not a violation. Removing the virtual modifier breaks overrides in derived types and changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; CA1063 has no code fix.

## From the book

The `Dispose(bool)` method is the one that should be overridden by subclasses.

```csharp
// bad design
public class DisposableResourceHolder : IDisposable {
  public virtual void Dispose() { ... }
  protected virtual void Dispose(bool disposing) { ... }
}

// good design
public class DisposableResourceHolder : IDisposable {
  public void Dispose() { ... }
  protected virtual void Dispose(bool disposing) { ... }
}
```

> **Brian Pepin:** If you look hard enough, there are still places in the framework where we don’t follow this pattern. By the time we finalized the `Dispose` pattern, quite a bit of the framework had already been written. Although we scrubbed everything to the best of our ability, a few things still slipped through the cracks.
